subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Effectiveness of AML Systems
description: A quick win: understand Effectiveness of AML Systems.

hook.text: The UN estimates only 1% of global money laundering is intercepted. $2 trillion flows unchecked every year.

buildup.text: Banks spend over $200 billion annually on AML compliance. The return on that investment is questionable.

discovery.text: Most AML effort goes to filing reports and checking boxes, not to actually stopping criminal money flows.

twist.text: Some experts argue that AML has become a compliance industry that protects banks, not society.

climax.text: The 1% interception rate suggests the system needs radical rethinking, not just more rules.

punchline.text: $200 billion spent. 1% caught. The math doesn't work.

quiz.question: What percentage of global money laundering is intercepted?
